tam-huu-tra-que.name: Tam Huu Tra Que Shrimp, Pork and Herb Rolls
tam-huu-tra-que.serving_basis: A small shared plate for four; serve as a starter or alongside a family meal.
tam-huu-tra-que.description: Each tam huu roll pairs a stir-fried river shrimp with a slice of boiled pork and fresh basil, tied with blanched scallion and served with sweet-sour fish sauce. The dish is associated with Tra Que vegetable village. Bếp Việt has adapted the quantities for four people; the recipe has not been test-cooked.
tam-huu-tra-que.finished_dish: Tender shrimp, soft pork and fragrant basil are bundled into bite-size rolls, with a balanced sweet-sour dip on the side.
tam-huu-tra-que.serving: Arrange the rolls on a plate and place the sweet-sour fish sauce in the middle. Serve while the shrimp and pork are still warm.
tips: Boil the pork until just cooked and let it cool slightly before slicing thinly.
Stir-fry the shrimp until opaque and fully cooked, but do not overcook it.
Briefly blanch the scallion strands until pliable and drain before tying the rolls.
search_terms: Tra Que shrimp pork herb rolls
tam-huu-tra-que.image_alt: A plate of Tra Que tam huu rolls made with cooked shrimp, boiled pork, basil and scallion, with dipping sauce.
tam-huu-tra-que.time_note: About 45 minutes; boiling time depends on the thickness of the pork.

ingredients.name: Medium river shrimp
ingredients.notes: Trim the antennae, devein and rinse.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Choose a balanced lean-to-fat cut for boiling.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese basil
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves, wash and drain.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Choose long strands to blanch and tie the rolls.

ingredients.name: Peanut oil
ingredients.notes: For stir-frying the shrimp; neutral oil can be substituted.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the dipping sauce to taste.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For boiling the pork and blanching scallions.

preparation_steps: Rinse the pork, shrimp and herbs separately. Trim and devein the shrimp; wash the basil and scallions and drain.
Bring salted water to a boil and cook the pork until fully done. Let it cool slightly, then slice thinly.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves; add chopped garlic and chili.
Briefly blanch the scallion strands until pliable, then drain.
cooking_steps: Heat the peanut oil and stir-fry the shrimp until pink-orange and fully cooked; let cool slightly.
Arrange a slice of pork, a basil leaf and one shrimp together, then tie into a small bundle with a blanched scallion strand.
Arrange on a plate and serve with the sweet-sour fish sauce.

canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.name: Quang Binh Stingray and Edible Cactus Soup
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.serving_basis: One shared pot of soup for a four-person family meal.
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.description: Stingray is simmered with young edible cactus pads, tamarind and herbs. The broth is gently sour with a mild natural bitterness from the cactus. Bếp Việt has adapted the vegetable quantities for a family serving; only use edible cactus from a verified food source, never ornamental or unidentified plants.
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.finished_dish: Tender stingray in a bright, gently sour broth; properly prepared cactus retains a tender-crisp texture with little slime.
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.serving: Ladle the fish, cactus and herbs into deep bowls, finish with rice paddy herb and cilantro, and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Use only young pads of a cactus sold for food; never use ornamental or unidentified cactus.
Remove spines and tough outer skin, slice thinly and blanch separately to reduce mucilage before cooking.
Cook the stingray completely through and add the herbs at the end.
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.image_alt: A bowl of Quang Binh stingray cactus soup with cooked fish, young cactus slices, okra, taro stem and herbs.
canh-ca-duoi-xuong-rong-quang-binh.time_note: About 70 minutes, including 15 minutes to season the fish; cactus preparation time may vary.

ingredients.name: Stingray
ingredients.notes: Clean thoroughly and cut into serving pieces.

ingredients.name: Young edible cactus pads
ingredients.notes: Remove spines and tough skin, then slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water and strain the pulp.

ingredients.name: Okra
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short pieces.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use for seasoning and the fish marinade.

preparation_steps: Rinse the stingray, cut into pieces and season with salt and pepper for about 15 minutes.
Use young edible cactus with clear food provenance. Remove spines and tough outer skin, slice thinly, blanch until less slimy, and drain.
Soak the tamarind in warm water and strain. Rinse and cut the okra and taro stem; chop the herbs and chili.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots until fragrant, add the stingray and gently sear the surface.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then simmer until the fish is fully cooked.
Add the blanched cactus, tamarind liquid, okra and taro stem. Cook until the vegetables are just tender; season with fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Turn off the heat, add rice paddy herb, cilantro and chili, and serve hot.

xoi-ram-ba-don.name: Ba Don Sticky Rice with Crispy Pork Rolls
xoi-ram-ba-don.serving_basis: Four servings of sticky rice with pork ram, suitable for breakfast or as a filling family dish.
xoi-ram-ba-don.description: Fluffy white sticky rice is served with small pork rolls wrapped in rice paper and fried until crisp. A local newspaper describes this as a familiar Ba Don pairing, often eaten with peanut salt or lime-garlic-chili fish sauce. Bếp Việt has adapted the quantities for four; the recipe has not been test-cooked.
xoi-ram-ba-don.finished_dish: Separate, tender sticky-rice grains accompany small golden ram rolls with a crisp shell and moist pork filling.
xoi-ram-ba-don.serving: Divide the hot sticky rice into small portions and eat with the ram rolls. Offer peanut salt or lime-garlic-chili fish sauce on the side.
tips: Soak the rice long enough and drain well before steaming for fluffy results.
Hand-chop the pork rather than grinding it finely, so the filling keeps some texture.
Fry the rolls over medium heat and turn often so the filling cooks before the wrappers darken.
search_terms: Ba Don sticky rice with crispy pork rolls
xoi-ram-ba-don.image_alt: A plate of Ba Don xoi ram with fluffy white sticky rice, golden pork rolls and a small bowl of peanut salt.
xoi-ram-ba-don.time_note: About 9 hours 15 minutes including overnight soaking; active kitchen time is about 75 minutes.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Choose fragrant grains and soak overnight.

ingredients.name: Rice-paper wrappers for ram
ingredients.notes: Soften according to the package directions.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the ram; the rolls absorb less than this amount.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the filling and peanut salt.

preparation_steps: Gently rinse the glutinous rice, soak in clean water for 6–8 hours or overnight, then drain well.
Hand-chop the pork and mix with shallot, seasoning powder, pepper and some of the salt; rest for about 15 minutes.
Lightly crush the roasted peanuts with the remaining salt.
cooking_steps: Spread the rice in a steamer and steam until tender and fully cooked. Gently fluff once partway through and keep covered.
Place a small amount of pork filling on each rice-paper wrapper, roll into a short ram and fold in the ends.
Fry the ram over medium heat, turning until golden and crisp and the pork filling is fully cooked. Drain on a rack.
Serve the hot sticky rice with ram and peanut salt; lime-garlic-chili fish sauce is optional.

nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.name: Tram Mushrooms Stir-Fried with Sweet Potato Shoots
aliases: Nam tram xao rau khoai lang
Tram mushroom and rau lang stir-fry
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.serving_basis: One shared stir-fry for four people at a family meal.
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.description: Tram mushrooms are stir-fried with sweet potato shoots and pork belly. A regional newspaper records this pairing and notes that tram mushrooms are enjoyed in some North-Central provinces; Bếp Việt does not generalize it to the entire region and has adapted the quantities for four people.
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.finished_dish: Tram mushrooms retain a gentle bitterness and lingering sweetness, while the greens stay tender and the pork is just cooked.
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.serving: Transfer to a wide plate and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Buy correctly identified tram mushrooms from a trusted seller; never forage unfamiliar wild mushrooms.
Wash soil from the stems carefully and blanch briefly if you prefer a milder bitterness; drain well.
Add the sweet potato shoots after the mushrooms and stir-fry only until tender to keep their color and avoid excess liquid.
search_terms: tram mushroom sweet potato shoot stir-fry
nam tram xao ngon rau khoai
nam tram xao rau khoai lang
North Central Vietnam mushroom stir fry
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.image_alt: A plate of tram mushrooms stir-fried with sweet potato shoots and pork belly.
nam-tram-xao-ngon-rau-khoai.time_note: About 35 minutes; briefly blanch the mushrooms first if you want a milder bitterness.

ingredients.name: Fresh tram mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Use correctly identified mushrooms and clean soil from them.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato shoots
ingredients.notes: Trim tough stems, rinse and cut into lengths.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For rinsing and blanching the mushrooms.

preparation_steps: Sort the mushrooms, trim soil-covered ends and rinse quickly several times. Briefly blanch if desired to soften the bitterness, then drain.
Pick and rinse the sweet potato shoots, discard tough parts and cut into lengths.
Thinly slice the pork belly and mince the shallots.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and stir-fry the pork until just firm and lightly rendered; add the shallots and cook until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry over medium heat until hot and most released liquid has evaporated.
Add the sweet potato shoots and toss until just tender. Season with fish sauce, salt and pepper; turn off the heat while the greens are still bright.

banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.name: Cua Tung Seaweed Jelly Cake
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.serving_basis: A light dish divided among four, served as a snack or side.
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.description: Coastal seaweed is simmered slowly until concentrated, then set into a soft, deep green jelly cake. The dish is documented at Cua Tung fish market in Quang Tri. Bếp Việt has adapted the quantities for four; use only food-grade seaweed from a safe supplier, never gather it from rocky shores yourself.
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.finished_dish: Deep green, tender seaweed jelly that can be cut into pieces; serve plain or with a little seasoned fermented shrimp paste.
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.serving: Let the jelly cool and set fully, cut into bite-size squares and serve chilled or at room temperature with the dip on the side.
tips: Choose seaweed sold for food and traceable to a safe supplier.
Rinse carefully with clean water and remove sand and debris; do not cook with untreated seawater.
Simmer gently and skim the foam often for a smoother set with fewer bubbles.
search_terms: banh duc rau cau Cua Tung
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.image_alt: A plate of deep green Cua Tung seaweed jelly cake cut into pieces with a small bowl of chili fermented shrimp paste.
banh-duc-rau-cau-cua-tung.time_note: About 3 hours 25 minutes including simmering and setting; the actual time depends on the seaweed.

ingredients.name: Fresh edible seaweed
ingredients.notes: Use a safe food-grade source and remove sand and debris.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For soaking and simmering the seaweed.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Crush and add to the soaking water.

ingredients.name: Fermented shrimp paste
ingredients.notes: For a small dipping sauce; choose a safely processed product.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Optional, to soften the salty flavor.

preparation_steps: Rinse the seaweed several times in clean water; pick out sand, shell fragments and debris, then drain.
Dissolve salt in water with crushed ginger, soak the seaweed briefly, rinse again and cut into shorter lengths.
Mix the fermented shrimp paste with a little warm water, sugar and lime juice; add chopped chili and set aside.
cooking_steps: Put the seaweed and water in a pot. Simmer gently until the strands soften and release their natural gel, stirring occasionally so they do not stick.
Skim the foam often. Strain out any tough strands if needed, then pour the concentrated seaweed mixture into a clean mold.
Let cool, chill until fully set, then cut into squares and serve with the fermented shrimp-paste dip.
